title: The interaction of the halo around the butterfly planetary nebula NGC 650-1 with the interstellar medium

evidence.locator: Abstract: "A SHAPE spatio-kinematical model indicates that NGC 650-1 has a broad central torus with an inclination angle of 75° with respect to the line of sight, whereas that of the bipolar lobes ... is 85°." Sect. 1: a distance of 0.93 ± 0.26 kpc (Frew, Parker & Bojičić 2016). Sect. 4.1: the equatorial ring has a size of about 95 arcsec and is oriented along position angle about 35°. Sect. 5: the main nebula is a thick equatorial ring that collimates two broad bipolar lobes; the bipolar axis is about 85° from the line of sight, the eastern lobe receding; de-projected velocities of 120 to 140 km/s for the lobes and about 37 km/s for the ring; a kinematical age of about 4760 yr at 0.93 kpc; a systemic LSR velocity of −22 km/s. Fig. 4: the model is shown as synthetic position-velocity maps only.
